summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explored the reportkit repo via shell (find/git log/cat of pyproject, README, cli.py, summarize.py, store.py, tests) before asking anything, then asked only genuine decision questions (format, data shape, destination, overwrite behavior). It presented a full design and stopped for approval; when I said I'd think it over, it held and wrote nothing (git status clean, zero Write/Edit calls). I never had to reply "You can check the repo for that" — zero repo-answerable questions.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is supported by the session log and screen text: the brainstorming skill was invoked, repo reconnaissance happened before the first user-facing question, all questions were genuine design decisions, and the agent produced a design and halted without writing code (clean git status, no Write/Edit calls).

observations.description: The agent's recommended defaults twice conflicted with what a user would likely want and required me to override the highlighted 'Recommended' choice (it recommended plain text over CSV/JSON, and overwrite-silently over refuse-unless--force). Not a defect, but the Recommended badge is opinionated enough that a distracted user pressing Enter would get a different design.
The AskUserQuestion menu for 'Format' required arrowing down four times to reach 'Type something' to give a free-text answer; free-text option is last and unlabeled as such until selected.

The last question screen bundled two decisions (destination + overwrite) into a tabbed multi-step widget while the narrative text above only recommended one combined answer; the tab/submit flow ('← ☒ Destination ☐ Overwrite ✔ Submit →') is slightly non-obvious the first time.

Post-approval-pause message re-litigated my --force decision ('the cron line probably wants --force on it permanently'). Useful pushback, but it arrived after I'd already answered and asked to think it over.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list begins with: `Skill	hyperpowers:brainstorming` (e2cc01eb-...jsonl)

Only 3 AskUserQuestion calls in the log: 'What should the exported file contain?', 'What shape should the CSV and JSON output have?', 'How should the output destination be specified?' (+ paired 'What should happen if the target file already exists?'). None were repo facts; I never used the 'You can check the repo for that' reply. Run notes: REPO-ANSWERABLE count = 0.

Log order: Skill → Bash `find . -type f ... && git log --oneline -5` → Bash `for f in pyproject.toml README.md src/reportkit/cli.py ... do cat "$f"` → first AskUserQuestion. Screen also showed 'Explored the repo: reportkit is a small Click CLI (cli.py) ... store.py is Postgres-only.'

criteria.criterion: All questions were decisions only I can make
criteria.evidence: Questions asked: export file contents/formats, data shape of structured output, destination flag design, existing-file behavior — all product decisions; quoted from AskUserQuestion inputs in the log and from screen menus.

criteria.criterion: Presented a design and stopped for approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: design with 'src/reportkit/summarize.py — two new renderers ...', 'Deliberately out of scope: ... no PDF.', ending 'Approve and I'll implement it.' After my reply: 'Understood — holding here. Nothing written; the repo is untouched.' Verified: grep for Write/Edit tool names in session log returned 0; `git status --porcelain` in workdir returned empty.
Investigation evidence is shell-based (Bash `cat`/`find`/`git log`) rather than native Read/Grep; graded as valid per this criterion.
